title: Unlock a pair of locked pruning shears in a blade guard so their handles spring open
instruction: Unlock the guarded pruners and leave their handles open.
context: Hand pruners are stored locked shut and unlocked before every gardening session. Many have a squeeze-release stopper, as on the ARS VS-8Z: pulling the locked handles apart only loads the catch harder, while a short extra squeeze frees it and the spring then opens the handles. Here the blades stay inside a rigid guard and no person is present.
setup: Positions in cm: x ahead of the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midline; heights above the table. Shears (loose, 220 g, after the ARS VS-8Z): 200 mm long, a 54 mm blade ahead of the pivot bolt and two red grips 16 mm wide running 60 to 146 mm behind it; 20 mm thick, lying flat. Each grip lies 10 degrees off the tool's axis when locked (grip-end centres 51 mm apart). The fixed half (grip, neck, hook blade) is 120 g; the moving half (grip, neck, cutting blade) is 85 g and turns about the pivot: stopped 4 degrees past locked when squeezed, 20 degrees open at its natural stop (grip ends 100 mm apart). Its return spring gives 0.6 N m locked and 0.4 N m fully open (about 7 N at the grips). The pivot nut stands 4 mm proud. Stopper: a 15 g steel plate pivoted on top of the fixed grip 125 mm behind the pivot. Its notch (3 mm deep, 0.3 mm play a side) sits over a 7 mm brass pin on top of the moving grip; the return spring holds the pin in the notch's floor. A light spring (about 0.009 N m) turns the plate 25 degrees off the pin once the pin is out of the notch. Stand (loose, 1.5 kg, dark grey): a rest 250 x 150 mm, 30 mm high, under the whole tool, with a rigid orange guard over the blades, 115 x 90 mm, roof 56 mm up, closed on both sides and the far end, open toward the handles; it covers the blades' whole sweep. Inside, two blocks hang from the roof either side of the pivot nut and two 8 mm blocks flank the hook blade, locating the tool with about 1 mm play. Lot A (the screenshot): pivot over (36.0, -3.0), blades pointing 20 degrees to the robot's right of straight ahead, handles toward the robot. Lot B: pivot over (40.0, 2.0), blades 25 degrees to the robot's left. The tool starts locked. Friction (static/dynamic): shears 0.6/0.5, stand 1.2/1.0. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end, except the never rules. 1.0: the stopper turned at least 15 degrees off its pin, the moving handle within 5 degrees of its opening stop, the tool in its rest (pivot within 8 mm and 5 degrees of its start, underside within 2 mm of the rest's top) and the stand within 8 mm and 3 degrees of its start. 0.5: the stopper off as above and the grip ends at least 10 mm further apart than when locked, but not 1.0. Both tiers also need, for 2 s: no gripper or finger tip surface within 5 mm of the shears or the stand, and every part still (under 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s). 0: anything else, including still locked, squeezed and held, the stopper off with the handles shut, or still held. Never rules, over the whole trial (any one scores 0): the handle more than 3 degrees open while the stopper is turned under 10 degrees (forced past the catch); the pivot more than 20 mm from its start, the tool more than 15 mm off its rest, or the stand moved more than 20 mm. A hand state that cannot be read gives no credit. Real trial: judged from a photo (stopper position, grip-end spacing, tool in its stand) and the video. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 600 steps (30 s at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: 1. Squeeze the handles shut, push the stopper back over the pin with a thumb and let go, so the pin rests in its notch. 2. Place the stand with its pivot point over (36.0, -3.0) and the guard pointing 20 degrees to the robot's right (lot A), or over (40.0, 2.0) pointing 25 degrees to its left (lot B). 3. Lay the shears flat in the stand, blades under the guard, the pivot nut between the two roof blocks, the hook blade between the two low blocks, stopper side up. Run trials on lots A and B in turn.
fidelity: Length, blade, mass and pack size are ARS's. Grip outline, the 120/85/15 g mass split, friction, the 20-degree opening, spring torques, squeeze travel and the stopper's notch-and-pin shape are estimates; the maker gives none. Rigid boxes and cylinders; grips straight; handle stops are joint limits. The guard and stand are a test fixture, not part of the product. Two lots stop one fixed motion, not a replay of both.
scores: Dream-1 run: lot A refused by the Dream API (it judged the open blades a hazard; they stay inside the guard); lot B 1.0; reported task score 1.0 rests on lot B alone. Demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B.
